note: Art this project did not generate. Every other PNG beside this file is rendered by
tools/sprites and re-rendered pixel for pixel by `npm run sprites:check`; a key declared
here is the exception, and declaring it is what makes it an exception rather than a file
nobody noticed. The owner's call of 2026-09-09 (docs/30, 'Art we did not generate') was
that sprites are commissioned to this project's own spec rather than bought as a pack, so
an authored key is held to the same canvas, the same anchor and the same published bounds
as the rig it stands beside -- `npm run godot:check:authored` is where that is mechanical.
The owner's call of 2026-09-17 (docs/30, 'The outpost pack, adopted') was the opposite for
a second batch: `godot/art/simplyzombies/` is a hand-made pack and it is adopted whole,
overwriting the generated art it replaces.
Read by two things, which is the whole point of it being a file rather than a list in code:
tools/sprites/build.py (so --check knows not to try to regenerate it) and
presentation/appearance.gd's `canvas_of` (so the renderer knows its shape). The two-copies
arrangement every other shape table in this project carries -- PAWN_KEYS in Python and in
GDScript, VEHICLE_FOOTPRINTS in both -- is what this replaces for authored art.
An entry may declare `source`: `{path, crop?, pad?}`, `path` relative to godot/ (the same
string as after res://). tools/sprites/build.py reproduces it -- crop, then pad, never
repainted or resized, godot/art/simplyzombies/STYLE.md's own rule for its mechanical steps
-- so `--check` holds a sourced key to decoded pixels the same way it holds a generated one,
and `python3 tools/sprites/build.py` can write it. A key with no `source` (every
commissioned one so far) keeps the existence-and-shape check only: nothing here can
reproduce a PNG an artist delivered by hand.
An entry may instead be a **family**: `members` names several keys that each carry their
own `source` and share the family's `canvas`. The family key itself is not a file -- it is
the one `reads` and `kind` are declared against, for art that is one declaration but many
pictures (a walk cycle's frames, a garment's four sides). `godot:check:authored`'s READS
lane judges a family by its family key; a member is never content-named on its own.
`kind` decides which bounds the gate holds a key to:
rig      a body. The published bounds in README.md: height, head, shoulders, clearance,
soles on the bottom row. The eight generated rigs are held to the same numbers
by the same lane, so the spec cannot drift from the art that already meets it.
overlay  a piece of equipment composited onto a body. WORN_LOOK_OK owns its fit.
tile     a tile-sized picture seen from above, centred on its ground point.
icon     an inventory picture: one item base seen from above on a 32x32 canvas, centred on
the ground point and drawn on the floor and on a bag plate (`godot:check:authored`'s ICON
lane; `godot:check:appearance`'s ITEMS lane owns the draw).
pack_rig / pack_overlay
a body that turns and walks, and a wearable that turns with it -- the outpost
pack's survivor and shambler, and its vest, helmet, gas mask and backpack.
`godot:check:authored`'s PACK lane judges both (since 2026-09-26).
pack_held
a weapon in the hand -- one of the outpost pack's held-weapon pictures, drawn
facing east at its own canvas (no crop, no pad) and turned per view by the
renderer (`Appearance.held_layer`). `grip` is a COPY of the pack manifest's
own grip point, the pixel that lands on the body's hand; `godot:check:authored`'s
HELD lane holds the copy, the canvas and the facing to the manifest (since
2026-09-26, 'Held weapons in the hand'). `muzzle` is a COPY of the manifest's muzzle
point, where a muzzle flash is drawn from ('The shot is seen'), held by the same lane.
sheet    one of the outpost pack's four-frame effect sheets, a family whose members
`<key>_0` .. `<key>_3` are the manifest's frames in order, cut whole. `fps`, `loop`
and `anchor` are COPIES of the manifest's own, and `godot:check:fx`'s RATE lane holds
them to it; presentation/fx_look.gd plays the sheet off sim events (since 2026-09-26,
'The shot is seen'). A sheet is read by a content effect field -- `fireFx`,
`casingFx`, `hitFx` or `flameFx` -- rather than a `sprite`.
module   placeholder for the outpost pack's walls slice -- wall modules. MANIFEST accepts
them today; no shape lane judges one yet, and it gains one when the walls slice
lands (docs/23's 'Art & renderer -- the outpost pack' group).
tree     a tall tree from the outpost pack, standing feet-anchored on its trunk tile in the
entity sort (docs/23's 'Trees, the bed and the heaps'). Cropped to the pack's
anchor row, never padded, so the picture's last row is the sole line and its
width is the canopy's own -- wider than the trunk's tile, which is the amendment
to 'one tile wide' docs/30's 'The outpost pack, adopted' makes.
prop     a pack picture drawn flat on a tile, under the bodies -- the bed, a heap on a Low
tile, a bush or a stump on open ground. Cropped to the anchor row like a tree and
hung with its last row on the tile's south edge (`Appearance.hang_rect`); never
more than a tile tall. `godot:check:authored`'s PICTURE lane is the shape lane
for both `tree` and `prop`.
vehicle  a parked car's east-west picture, from the outpost pack (docs/23's 'The cars
are the pack's, east-west'). Cropped to its anchor row, never padded, so the
renderer's feet anchor is the pack's own. check_wrecks.gd's PACK lane is its
shape lane: the painted span sets the class's `lEw`, and nothing else does.
`reads` names what draws it -- a content id whose appearance block declares the key. Art
nothing reads is the dead-socket shape this project has paid for twelve times, so the gate
refuses a key that names nothing rather than letting it sit here looking finished. Since
2026-09-17 `reads` only has to be ONE of the content ids that declare the key, not the last
one loaded -- two bases sharing one icon are both allowed to claim it.
A **cells** source is the other shape a `source` can take: `cells` in place of `path`, each
cell one whole pack picture pasted at `at: [x, y]` on the entry's canvas, with the files in
`over` alpha-composited onto it first -- the layering the renderer would do per frame, done
once. Never cropped, resized or recoloured; build.py refuses a cell that runs off the canvas or
overlaps another. Kind `ground` is the one cells source so far: `ground_atlas`, composed from the
pack's terrain tiles and grass fringes (docs/23, 'The ground is the pack's', 2026-09-27).
Its `reads` is not a content id -- no content entry names the ground -- but
`<file>:<function>`, the renderer function that blits it, and `godot:check:authored`'s READS
lane holds that function to calling `Appearance.ground_atlas(`.
Optional `anchor: [x, y]` (pixels) and `palette: "generator"|"pack"` are accepted by
MANIFEST. `anchor` has two readers: PICTURE (a `tree` or `prop` says where it stands and the
lane holds it to the pack's own), and the renderer for a sheet (the pixel of each frame that
lands on the muzzle, the chest or the fire); `palette` is read by nothing yet.
A family that TURNS names its members by one convention, and the renderer finds them by it
(presentation/appearance.gd's `frame_key`): `<family>_<view>` is the picture standing still
facing s, e, n or w, and `<family>_walk_<view>_<frame>` is one frame of the walk that way.
`resolve(<family>)` answers the `_s` member, the picture a body at rest shows, so a content
entry names the family key exactly as it would name one file. Two more fields, each a COPY
of the pack's own `godot/art/simplyzombies/manifest.json`, because the renderer never loads
that file (a runtime reader of the pack would be a second path to the art) and the gate is
what holds the copy to it (`godot:check:authored`'s PACK lane):
fps  the walk's frames per second, a pack_rig's `fps.walk`; the frame is chosen from
`world.tick` with integer arithmetic, so it is the same on every machine.
z    per view, a pack_overlay's `z_by_direction`; below zero it draws under the body, which
is how the backpack hangs behind a body seen from the side.
Every member is cropped 32x48 -> 32x40 on the pack's own anchor row (the soles stay on row
39); what the crop drops is only the pack's sub-visible specks, and PACK proves that too.
